summary: I found two problems with this PR. It records a step-by-step trace of each agent run (prompts, model replies, reasoning summaries, tool calls and results, tokens and timing per turn), writes it to its own JSON file next to the run record, and asks Anthropic for summarized reasoning. The trace code itself looks correct. First, the request change probably switches on extended thinking for every review, not only its display, which changes cost and how often replies get cut off. Second, the trace is lost in exactly the crashed runs where it would help most. The new trace code also has no tests.

accepted.title: Asking for reasoning summaries probably also turns on extended thinking for every review
accepted.whatGoesWrong: Before this PR the request set no thinking option, so as far as I can tell the model answered without extended thinking. Setting an adaptive thinking config most likely turns thinking on, not just its display. If so, every turn now spends extra output tokens on reasoning, and those tokens count toward the 16,000-token reply limit. A long review turn is then more likely to stop with max_tokens, which ends the run as TRUNCATED, and no review is posted.
accepted.whyItMatters: A change meant only for logging would quietly change how the reviewer behaves. It would raise the cost of every PR review and could cause reviews that worked before to fail.
accepted.howToFix: Check the API docs to confirm whether this setting enables thinking or only changes how it is shown. If it enables thinking, make that a deliberate, configurable choice: for example a constructor flag that is off by default. Raise maxTokens to leave room for thinking, and note the expected cost change in the PR.

accepted.title: The trace is lost when a run crashes, which is when it is most needed
accepted.whatGoesWrong: The trace is built in a local list and only handed out in the AgentResult when run() returns normally. Suppose the Anthropic call fails partway through, for example with a network error, a rate limit or a 5xx. The exception then leaves run() and main(), and nothing is written to review-agent/runs/. The CI 'Upload run record' step then finds no files.
accepted.whyItMatters: The trace exists to explain afterwards what went wrong in a run. Crashed runs are the ones that most need explaining, and right now they leave no trace at all.
accepted.howToFix: Catch provider exceptions in run() and return an AgentResult with a failure outcome, the error message and the trace so far. Alternatively, have main write the trace in a finally block, or stream entries to disk as they are recorded. Add a unit test with a fake provider that throws on turn 2, and check that the turn-1 entries are still saved.
